steps.instruction: Heat 1 tbsp sunflower oil in a medium saucepan, then soften 1 chopped onion and 2-3 chopped carrots for a few mins.
When soft, turn up the heat, crumble in 500g lamb mince and brown, tipping off any excess fat.
Add 2 tbsp tomato purée and a large splash of Worcestershire sauce, then fry for a few mins.
Pour over 500ml beef stock, bring to a simmer, then cover and cook for 40 mins, uncovering halfway.

Meanwhile, heat the oven to 180C/fan 160C/gas 4, then make the mash. Boil the 900g potato, cut into chunks, in salted water for 10-15 mins until tender. Drain, then mash with 85g butter and 3 tbsp milk.
Put the mince into an ovenproof dish, top with the mash and ruffle with a fork. The pie can now be chilled and frozen for up to a month.

Bake for 20-25 mins until the top is starting to colour and the mince is bubbling through at the edges. (To bake from frozen, cook at 160C/fan 140C/gas 3 for 1 hr-1 hr 20 mins until piping hot in the centre. Flash under the grill to brown, if you like.)
Leave to stand for 5 mins before serving.

菜名：牧羊人派
1. Heat 1 tbsp sunflower oil in a medium saucepan, then soften 1 chopped onion and 2-3 chopped carrots for a few mins.
2. When soft, turn up the heat, crumble in 500g lamb mince and brown, tipping off any excess fat.
3. Add 2 tbsp tomato purée and a large splash of Worcestershire sauce, then fry for a few mins.
4. Pour over 500ml beef stock, bring to a simmer, then cover and cook for 40 mins, uncovering halfway.
5. Meanwhile, heat the oven to 180C/fan 160C/gas 4, then make the mash. Boil the 900g potato, cut into chunks, in salted water for 10-15 mins until tender. Drain, then mash with 85g butter and 3 tbsp milk.
6. Put the mince into an ovenproof dish, top with the mash and ruffle with a fork. The pie can now be chilled and frozen for up to a month.
7. Bake for 20-25 mins until the top is starting to colour and the mince is bubbling through at the edges. (To bake from frozen, cook at 160C/fan 140C/gas 3 for 1 hr-1 hr 20 mins until piping hot in the centre. Flash under the grill to brown, if you like.)
8. Leave to stand for 5 mins before serving.

- Kosher salt

- 2 packets unflavored gelatin (about 14 g)

- 2 1/2 pounds (1 kg) ground lamb (the source also permits beef or a combination)
- 1 large yellow onion (400 g), diced
- 3 medium carrots (225 g), diced
- 2 ribs celery (110 g), diced
- 2 medium cloves garlic, minced
- 2 tablespoons (30 ml) tomato paste
- 1 cup (240 ml) dry red wine
- 2 sprigs thyme
- 1 bay leaf
- 1 tablespoon (15 ml) Worcestershire sauce
- 1 teaspoon (5 ml) Marmite, optional
- 2 tablespoons (15 g) all-purpose flour
- 8 ounces (225 g) frozen peas
- Freshly ground black pepper
- 1 1/2 cups (360 ml) heavy cream
- Grated Parmigiano-Reggiano for topping, optional

1. Rinse the cubed potatoes until the water runs clear, cover with cold salted water, simmer until tender, then drain and rinse with hot water.（10 to 15 minutes）【medium-low heat】
2. Mash the potatoes with butter, smooth the surface and cover directly to prevent a skin from forming.
3. Sprinkle gelatin over the chicken stock and set aside.
4. Brown half the lamb in hot oil, add the remaining lamb and break it into small bits, then remove excess fat and add onion, carrots, celery and garlic until they begin to soften.（about 13 to 15 minutes total）【high heat】
5. Cook tomato paste for 1 minute, add red wine and reduce almost fully; add stock, thyme, bay, Worcestershire and optional Marmite, stir in flour and simmer until thick. Remove herbs, stir in peas and season.（about 20 minutes）【low heat】
6. Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Simmer the cream, fold it into the mashed potatoes and season.【425°F / 220°C】
7. Place the meat sauce in a 9-by-13-inch baking dish, cover completely with mashed potatoes, texture the top and add Parmesan if desired.
